thread:
Priya (docs): quick sync: found inconsistent naming across the Dedicated provisioning guide and examples. seems a recent change renamed reserved_level -> commit_level in the backend and some examples s/safe_commit/commit_level/. customers copying examples will hit validation.
Derek (eng-platform): where are the offenders?
Priya (docs): examples: /docs/dedicated/provisioning.md, /docs/examples/terraform/reserved-pool.tf, and the python quickstart under /docs/sdk/python/. Also anchors to #isolation-guarantee now live at #isolation-level.
Anya (sdk): backend rename was intentional (semantics clearer). SDK v0.9 exposes commit_level but we added a shim mapping reserved_level -> commit_level for one release. docs should show commit_level and call out compatibility.
Luca (prod): customers love copy-paste. prefer canonical API in docs. add a brief compatibility note so older SDK users know the mapping.
Priya (docs): i drafted a tiny patch: change examples to commit_level, update terraform snippet to use commit_level = "standard", and add a migration table. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/612 (branch: docs/commit-level-unify).
Anya (sdk): i'll update the python snippet to the new arg name and include a compatibility snippet for SDK < v0.9 showing the old param mapping. suggestion:
```python
# canonical (v0.9+)
client.create_reserved_pool(region="us-west-2", capacity=4, commit_level="guaranteed")

# compatibility (older SDKs):
# reserved_level="guaranteed" -> commit_level="guaranteed"
```
Derek (eng-platform): i can add short 301 redirect files for the old anchor names so external links don't 404. also will confirm with infra if commit_level affects eviction heuristics wording.
Priya (docs): thanks. also found SLA table column 'isolation_guarantee' still used in the matrix; want to rename to 'isolation_level' for consistency. adding tooltip: "isolation_level indicates the operational isolation tier; not an absolute eviction immunity."
Luca (prod): good. also request: please add a one-line note under Reserved pools describing behavior when commit_level=guaranteed vs best_effort (customers ask about performance/cost tradeoffs).
Priya (docs): drafting language: "commit_level=guaranteed prioritizes tenant placement and reduces eviction probability at higher cost; best_effort favors lower cost but higher eviction risk." sanity-check?
Anya (sdk): accurate. i'll include a short code comment in the snippet showing the tradeoff.
preview-bot: preview build created: https://deploy-preview.redwood-docs.net/612  (validator warnings: examples/terraform/reserved-pool.tf unknown field 'reserved_level' at line 8).
Priya (docs): fixed terraform file in branch to use commit_level. i also added the migration table and a changelog entry.
Derek (eng-platform): anchors redirected and infra confirmed commit_level influences soft-preempt ordering only. adding sentence in docs: "commit_level influences soft-preempt ordering; it does not change hard preemption thresholds."
Anya (sdk): pushed snippet commit and compatibility note to the PR branch. requested reviews from @Derek and @Luca.
Luca (prod): reviewed wording and the SLA matrix rename. lgtm. tiny copyedit suggestion on the tradeoff sentence which i left inline on the PR.
Priya (docs): merged after approvals and published. created follow-up ticket for tenant-eviction flow diagram: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/DTX-1277. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
